title: Deployment-mode IAM onboarding cookbook and audit schema
content:
Purpose:
This is a hands-on cookbook for onboarding and validating IAM (RBAC v2) across Redwood deployment modes: Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved GPU), and Private (VPC/on-prem). It combines a lightweight role matrix, ready-to-copy policy templates, a standardized audit-log schema for SIEM export, and a minimal evidence-automation checklist for compliance reviews.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target audience: engineers (platform, infra), security reviewers, solutions engineers doing customer onboarding.
- Covers environment-by-environment recommended roles, example least-privilege policies, SIEM field mappings, and automation notes for evidence collection.
- Not a replacement for org-level IAM policies (cloud provider-specific root policies), but a practical layer mapped to Redwood service concepts.

Quick design principles (RBAC v2):
1) Role-focused: keep roles stable and scope with resource tags (project, customer-id).
2) Deployment-aware: minimal default perms in Hosted, stricter network and KMS separation in Private, predictable service accounts in Dedicated.
3) Audit-first: every role change or policy binding must produce an immutable audit event (actor, rationale, ticket).
4) Automate evidence: scriptable exports into the evidence bucket with manifest + checksum.

Role matrix (concise):
Columns: Role, Hosted (recommended), Dedicated (recommended), Private (recommended), Notes
- Viewer: read-only API console + logs; Hosted: yes; Dedicated: yes; Private: yes; For SRE/monitoring teams only.
- Operator: deploy/scale runtime, restart tasks; Hosted: limited (no tenant-level creds); Dedicated: yes; Private: yes; Scoped to cluster/namespace.
- ModelAdmin: upload model artifact, create model version, validate perf; Hosted: restricted (review pipeline); Dedicated: yes; Private: yes; Requires artifact store write + model registry perms.
- KMSAdmin: manage encryption keys; Hosted: no (managed by Redwood by default); Dedicated: optional; Private: yes; Only for customers with customer-managed KMS.
- NetworkAdmin: VPC, firewall rules; Hosted: no; Dedicated: limited; Private: yes; Private deployments must separate this role from ModelAdmin.
- BillingAdmin: view usage/billing; Hosted: yes (tenant-billing only); Dedicated: yes; Private: yes; Audit-enabled.
- AuditReader: read access to full audit logs + SIEM exports; Hosted: yes; Dedicated: yes; Private: yes; For compliance/forensic teams only.
- SupportEscalation: temporary elevated access through just-in-time (JIT) flow; Hosted: gated; Dedicated: gated; Private: gated; Requires ticket and 2FA.

Example permission sets (plain-language):
- Minimal Viewer: list applications, read metrics, read model metadata, read logs. No write, no secret access.
- Deployment Operator: create/update deployment resources, read logs, restart nodes, but cannot access KMS or modify network config.
- Model Admin: write to model registry, trigger model rollouts, read rollout status, cannot alter infra settings.

Policy templates (copy-and-edit):
Note: below are canonical policy statements; replace RESOURCE_ARNS/PROJECT_TAGS before use.

1) Hosted - model-read-only policy (JSON snippet as plain text):
{
  "Version": "2024-01-01",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "redwood:model:Get*",
        "redwood:model:List*"
      ],
      "Resource": ["arn:redwood:model:REGION:ACCOUNT:project/PROJECT_ID/*"]
    }
  ]
}

2) Dedicated - operator policy (plain text):
- Allow: cluster:Describe, cluster:UpdateScale, tasks:Restart, logs:Read, metrics:Read
- Deny: kms:CreateKey, network:ModifyFirewall, billing:ModifyInvoice

3) Private - separation-of-duties policy notes:
- Bind NetworkAdmin role to separate principals (network team service account) with MFA-enforced console access.
- KMS administration requires out-of-band approval (ticket reference in binding metadata).

Audit log schema (core fields for SIEM export):
We standardize a minimal, required event shape emitted by Redwood control plane and forwarders. Each exported event must include these fields (flattened JSON):
- event_id: unique event UUID
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601 timestamp in UTC
- actor_principal: canonical principal (user:<email> | svc:<service-account>)
- actor_role: the RBAC role at time of action (e.g., ModelAdmin)
- action: canonical action name (e.g., model.create, deployment.scale, kms.rotate_key)
- resource_type: e.g., model, deployment, key, network-rule
- resource_id: canonical resource identifier
- environment: hosted | dedicated | private
- result: success | failure | partial
- request_id: upstream request id (if applicable)
- ip_address: source IP (if available)
- change_summary: brief human-friendly summary of change (string)
- justification_ticket: linked Jira/Change ticket id (if provided)
- correlation_id: optional for tracing multi-step operations
- before_snapshot: short JSON-string of pre-change critical fields (optional)
- after_snapshot: short JSON-string of post-change critical fields (optional)
- evidence_refs: list of evidence file URIs exported for audits (comma-separated)

SIEM field mapping guidance:
- Map event_id -> ecs.event.id or equivalent.
- timestamp_utc -> @timestamp (UTC).
- actor_principal -> user.name, actor_role -> user.roles.
- action -> event.action, resource_type/resource_id -> resource.identifier/resource.type.
- justification_ticket -> labels.ticket_id for quick lookup in dashboards.

Export cadence and retention (recommendation):
- Real-time export (stream) for high-risk actions (kms.*, network.*) into SIEM ingest endpoint.
- Batched export (hourly) for lower-risk operations (model inference metrics, non-admin reads).
- Retention: raw events 365 days in SIEM hot/cold tiers; compressed backup of daily manifests for 7 years in evidence archive if requested by compliance.

Evidence automation playbook (minimal viable):
1) Trigger points: role binding changes, policy updates, key rotations, network rule changes, customer onboarding completions.
2) Automation steps (scripted):
   - Collect current binding snapshot (cloud IAM API) -> write to evidence-bucket/<env>/<date>/bindings.json
   - Collect audit events for the window -> write to evidence-bucket/<env>/<date>/events.ndjson
   - Generate manifest (CSV) linking files and compute SHA256 checksums -> upload manifest.json
   - Create meta-ticket with links (use jira API) and post to #sec-ops channel with archive link.
3) Minimal script example (pseudocode):
   - curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $SVC_TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/iam/bindings?env=private > bindings.json
   - aws s3 cp bindings.json s3://evidence-arch/private/2025-09-10/bindings.json
   - python3 build_manifest.py --dir s3://evidence-arch/private/2025-09-10 --out manifest.json

Just-in-time (JIT) elevation pattern for SupportEscalation role:
- Use a TTL-limited temporary credential system integrated with SSO (Ory/Okta) and approval webhook.
- Every JIT grant must create an audit event with fields: approver, approver_ticket, ttl_seconds, reason.
- Automated revocation enforced by control plane and verified by nightly scan.

Operational checks (pre-onboarding checklist):
- [ ] Confirm environment tag conventions (project/customer-id) exist and used in policies.
- [ ] Ensure KMS key access is limited and key aliases documented for private deployments.
- [ ] Verify SIEM ingestion endpoints and credentials for team can receive events.
- [ ] Confirm retention and backup policy signed off by compliance for customer.
- [ ] Validate JIT workflow with SSO and test one successful escalation + auto-revoke.

Common pitfalls and mitigations:
- Overbroad 'operator' role: mitigate by splitting into 'operator-runtime' and 'operator-deploy' with narrower scopes.
- Missing ticket links in audit events: enforce through pre-binding webhook that rejects changes without justification_ticket metadata.
- Evidence gaps in private/on-prem: ensure local forwarder runs with buffer and retry to central archive (no direct internet write from air-gapped without approved transfer protocol).

Open questions / items for follow-up:
- Decide canonical length for retained 'before_snapshot' / 'after_snapshot' to balance PII risk and forensic utility. (Security + Legal)
- Template for service-account lifecycle (rotate creds cadence) to be harmonized across Dedicated and Private. (Infra)

Appendix: useful references and quick commands
- Confluence onboarding checklist: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/SCC/IAM-Onboarding
- GitHub infra automation PR to reuse: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-automation/pull/678
- Jira change template: JIRA-1234

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a pragmatic, copy-friendly doc for engineering teams to adapt. Please review the policy snippets for provider-specific syntax and replace RESOURCE placeholders before applying.
- If accepted, next step: convert minimal pieces into Terraform modules and add CI checks that validate audit schema presence on any binding change.

-- Maya
